name: Stafflancer Outreach
author: stafflancerdev

sections.description:
Stafflancer Outreach helps you plan cold email outreach, organize contacts, and manage scheduled follow-ups directly in WordPress. Build multi-step email sequences, connect sender inboxes, review messages, and monitor sending activity without switching between tools.

For sales outreach, service introductions, and follow-ups with potential clients, the controlled Queue follows your configured sending schedules, inbox limits, pause controls, and recipient-safety checks.

Keep your contacts organized

  • Add or import contacts and organize them into groups.
  • Search by name, email, company, or position and manage contacts with bulk actions.
  • Repair missing first names from your original CSV files with a preview of exact email matches before applying changes. Existing names and other contact details are preserved.

Create email sequences and follow-ups

  • Write multi-step outreach sequences with follow-up messages.
  • Build A/B email variants and preview both HTML and plain-text messages.
  • Configure sending schedules, select sender inboxes, and review your sequence before it starts.

Write with more confidence

The included Free Writing Assistant helps you turn your offer and audience details into outreach messages you can review and refine.

  • Generate and regenerate suggested email copy using built-in, reviewed writing blocks.
  • Get a Writing Score for drafts you write yourself or create with the assistant.
  • Review suggestions before replacing your draft, and use Undo if you change your mind.
  • Add optional links, choose from supported writing tones, and keep your own wording and locked content.

The Writing Assistant does not require an external AI account, subscription, or paid generation service. Suggested writing is currently generated in English, while the plugin interface supports translation.

Connect the inboxes you already use

  • Connect manual SMTP, Gmail or Google Workspace, and Outlook or Microsoft 365.
  • Send test emails and check inbox and domain readiness.
  • Keep separate sender identities, signatures, sending limits, and activity for each configured inbox.

The Free edition has no commercial sender-inbox count cap. You remain responsible for any limits imposed by your email provider or hosting setup.

Stay in control of every send

Outreach uses a reviewable sending Queue instead of unrestricted bulk sending.

  • See what is scheduled, review projected sending times, and monitor Sending Activity.
  • Set sending windows, respect inbox limits, and pause sequences when needed.
  • Use Recipient Safety suppressions to avoid future Queue sends to affected contacts. Supported Gmail and Microsoft inbox connections can detect eligible replies and bounces when the required mailbox access is configured.
  • Check Queue Diagnostics and readiness guidance before enabling automatic sending.

The Free edition does not include open or click tracking or signed-unsubscribe functionality. Always follow applicable email, privacy, and anti-spam requirements.

Find your way around with ease

Use the Daily Pulse dashboard to see your outreach at a glance. The Launch Setup checklist, built-in User Manual, deliverability guidance, and Queue Diagnostics help you set up your workspace and understand the next action to take.

Start free, add Pro when you need it

All features included in Stafflancer Outreach Free work without a license key. Stafflancer Outreach Pro is an optional, separately distributed commercial add-on that requires a compatible Stafflancer Outreach Free/Core installation. Pro is not included in the WordPress.org download.

Learn more: https://plugin.stafflancer.com/product/stafflancer-outreach/

External services

Stafflancer Outreach Free does not send analytics or telemetry to Stafflancer and does not contact Stafflancer servers automatically. External requests occur only when an administrator explicitly configures or uses a feature that requires an email provider, the optional Feedback service, or DNS diagnostics.

Stafflancer Feedback service

Service: https://plugin.stafflancer.com/

Purpose and data: when an authorized user presses Submit feedback, the plugin sends the selected feedback type, subject, message, Outreach version, installed Pro version when available, and distribution channel. The user may separately provide an email address, request one transactional copy, allow Stafflancer to contact them, and opt in to basic diagnostics. Optional diagnostics can include WordPress, PHP, Outreach and Pro versions, distribution channel, locale, and browser identifier. The form does not send the site URL, OAuth/access tokens, license keys, recipient/contact lists, inbox credentials, or campaign email bodies.

Privacy: https://plugin.stafflancer.com/privacy-policy/
Terms: https://plugin.stafflancer.com/terms-and-conditions/

Administrator-configured SMTP server

Purpose and data: when an administrator configures a manual SMTP inbox, the plugin connects directly to that chosen SMTP server for a requested test email or Queue send. SMTP authentication sends the configured username and password/app password to that provider. A send transmits the sender and recipient addresses, subject, message body, standard email headers, and normal SMTP connection data. The SMTP password is stored encrypted in WordPress and is not sent to Stafflancer.

Terms and privacy depend on the SMTP provider selected by the administrator. Administrators should review that provider’s policies before connecting it.

Google OAuth2 and Gmail API

Purpose and data: an administrator can connect Gmail or Google Workspace with OAuth2. Google receives the configured OAuth client ID, redirect URI, requested scopes, one-time state and OIDC nonce values, authorization code or refresh token as required by the OAuth flow, and the credentials needed for token exchange. Queue sending sends the sender/recipient addresses, subject, message body, threading headers, and OAuth authorization to Gmail. Public signing keys are fetched from Google over HTTPS to validate connection identity. Diagnostics can query account identity. When mailbox-read access is enabled, Recipient Safety can issue bounded mailbox searches using sender/contact addresses, send-time boundaries, and/or a prior message ID to classify replies and delivery failures. Raw mailbox bodies are not stored by this scanner; only local suppression and bounded detection evidence are retained.

Google terms/privacy: https://developers.google.com/workspace/terms
Google API user-data policy: https://developers.google.com/terms/api-services-user-data-policy
Google privacy: https://policies.google.com/privacy

Microsoft OAuth2 and Microsoft Graph

Purpose and data: an administrator can connect Outlook or Microsoft 365 with OAuth2. Microsoft receives the configured OAuth client ID, redirect URI, requested scopes, one-time state and OIDC nonce values, selected tenant/account mode, authorization code or refresh token, and credentials needed for token exchange. Queue sending sends sender/recipient addresses, subject, message body, standard/threading headers, and OAuth authorization to Microsoft Graph. Microsoft OpenID configuration and public signing keys are fetched over HTTPS to validate connection identity. Diagnostics can query account identity. With Mail.Read enabled, Recipient Safety can query a bounded set of recent messages and process fields needed to classify replies and delivery failures; only local suppression and bounded detection evidence are stored.

Microsoft API terms: https://learn.microsoft.com/legal/microsoft-apis/terms-of-use
Microsoft privacy: https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/privacy/privacystatement

DNS resolver used by Inbox Diagnostics

Purpose and data: when an administrator runs inbox/domain diagnostics, PHP DNS lookups can check SPF, DKIM, DMARC, MX, TXT, and CNAME records for the configured sender domain. DNS requests contain only the domain or host name being checked and use the server’s configured DNS resolver. No contact list, email body, SMTP password, or OAuth token is included. Resolver terms/privacy depend on the site’s hosting or network provider.

Privacy and data

No analytics or telemetry is collected by Stafflancer Outreach or sent to Stafflancer. The plugin stores outreach workspace data in the site’s WordPress database, including contacts, groups, inbox configuration, sequence drafts, Queue records, send records, Recipient Safety suppressions, diagnostics, and OAuth2 setup/token metadata when configured.

Inbox Diagnostics can perform DNS lookups for the selected sender domain, including SPF, DKIM, DMARC, and MX records, using the site server’s configured DNS resolver. These lookups are performed only for inbox/domain diagnostics and are not sent to Stafflancer.

Sensitive SMTP secrets and provider OAuth credentials/tokens are stored using the plugin’s encrypted storage helpers. OAuth access is used only for the connected email-provider functions described above. Site administrators remain responsible for configuring their email providers appropriately, obtaining any required permissions or consent, and following applicable email, privacy, and anti-spam rules.

Source Code

The JavaScript and CSS source files for this plugin are included in this
download, under assets/js/ and assets/css/ respectively. The main application
script is assets/js/app-shell.js.

These files are maintained as plain JavaScript and CSS and are served directly
by the plugin. No compilation, bundling, or minification step is required to
modify or run them. Edit the included source files to make changes; no separate
source download or access to a development repository is required.

First-name repair

In Contacts, choose Repair missing names and upload the original CSV files. Preview exact email matches before filling blank first names. Existing names and all other contact details, groups, sequences and queue rows are kept. Download the report before leaving. Previews and reports are private to the current account and sign-in, expire after 24 hours, and expired preview records are removed when accessed or when that account creates a new preview. Completed repair outcomes are also recorded in the existing local audit log. CSV data is not sent to an external service. No hosting or cron configuration changes are required.
sections.installation:
1. In your WordPress dashboard, open Plugins > Add New, find Stafflancer Outreach, and install and activate it.
  2. Open Outreach from the WordPress admin menu and follow the Launch Setup checklist.
  3. Add contacts or import a CSV, then organize your contacts into groups.
  4. Connect an SMTP, Gmail, or Microsoft sender inbox and send a test email.
  5. Create an email sequence, review the messages and sending schedule, and check Queue readiness before enabling automatic sending.
sections.faq:
Is Stafflancer Outreach free to use?

Yes. Every feature included in Stafflancer Outreach Free works without a license key. Pro is an optional add-on sold separately.

Can I send email through Gmail, Outlook, or my own SMTP server?

Yes. Connect Gmail or Google Workspace, Outlook or Microsoft 365, or a manual SMTP inbox. Sending uses the selected, configured inbox and remains subject to Queue safeguards, schedules, and provider limits.

Can Outreach send follow-up emails automatically?

Yes. When automatic sending is enabled, the Queue can send scheduled sequence messages within the saved sending windows and inbox limits. Pause controls and Recipient Safety checks continue to apply.

Do I need an external AI service to use the Writing Assistant?

No. The included Writing Assistant uses reviewed, built-in writing blocks. It can suggest messages, score drafts, and help you revise copy without requiring an external AI account or paid generation service. Suggested writing is currently in English.

Can I import contacts from a spreadsheet?

Yes. You can import contacts from CSV files, organize them into groups, and use a preview-first tool to fill missing first names from your original CSVs using exact email matches.

What happens when a contact replies or an email bounces?

Recipient Safety can suppress contacts from future Queue sends through manual status controls and supported Gmail or Microsoft reply/bounce detection when the necessary mailbox access is configured.

Does the Free edition include open and click tracking?

No. Free does not include open or click tracking or signed-unsubscribe functionality. Reply and bounce checks through supported connected inboxes are separate recipient-safety features.

Is my contact list sent to Stafflancer?

No. Stafflancer Outreach does not automatically send analytics or telemetry to Stafflancer. Contacts and sequences are stored in your WordPress database. Sending uses the email provider you configure, and optional feedback is submitted only when you choose to send it. See External services and Privacy and data below for details.

  • Review suggestions before replacing your draft, and use Undo if you change your mind.
  • Add optional links, choose from supported writing tones, and keep your own wording and locked content.

The Writing Assistant does not require an external AI account, subscription, or paid generation service. Suggested writing is currently generated in English, while the plugin interface supports translation.

Connect the inboxes you already use

  • Connect manual SMTP, Gmail or Google Workspace, and Outlook or Microsoft 365.
  • Send test emails and check inbox and domain readiness.
  • Keep separate sender identities, signatures, sending limits, and activity for each configured inbox.

The Free edition has no commercial sender-inbox count cap. You remain responsible for any limits imposed by your email provider or hosting setup.

Stay in control of every send

Outreach uses a reviewable sending Queue instead of unrestricted bulk sending.

  • See what is scheduled, review projected sending times, and monitor Sending Activity.
  • Set sending windows, respect inbox limits, and pause sequences when needed.
  • Use Recipient Safety suppressions to avoid future Queue sends to affected contacts. Supported Gmail and Microsoft inbox connections can detect eligible replies and bounces when the required mailbox access is configured.
  • Check Queue Diagnostics and readiness guidance before enabling automatic sending.

The Free edition does not include open or click tracking or signed-unsubscribe functionality. Always follow applicable email, privacy, and anti-spam requirements.

Find your way around with ease

Use the Daily Pulse dashboard to see your outreach at a glance. The Launch Setup checklist, built-in User Manual, deliverability guidance, and Queue Diagnostics help you set up your workspace and understand the next action to take.

Start free, add Pro when you need it

All features included in Stafflancer Outreach Free work without a license key. Stafflancer Outreach Pro is an optional, separately distributed commercial add-on that requires a compatible Stafflancer Outreach Free/Core installation. Pro is not included in the WordPress.org download.

Learn more: https://plugin.stafflancer.com/product/stafflancer-outreach/

External services

Stafflancer Outreach Free does not send analytics or telemetry to Stafflancer and does not contact Stafflancer servers automatically. External requests occur only when an administrator explicitly configures or uses a feature that requires an email provider, the optional Feedback service, or DNS diagnostics.

Stafflancer Feedback service

Service: https://plugin.stafflancer.com/

Purpose and data: when an authorized user presses Submit feedback, the plugin sends the selected feedback type, subject, message, Outreach version, installed Pro version when available, and distribution channel. The user may separately provide an email address, request one transactional copy, allow Stafflancer to contact them, and opt in to basic diagnostics. Optional diagnostics can include WordPress, PHP, Outreach and Pro versions, distribution channel, locale, and browser identifier. The form does not send the site URL, OAuth/access tokens, license keys, recipient/contact lists, inbox credentials, or campaign email bodies.

Privacy: https://plugin.stafflancer.com/privacy-policy/
Terms: https://plugin.stafflancer.com/terms-and-conditions/

Administrator-configured SMTP server

Purpose and data: when an administrator configures a manual SMTP inbox, the plugin connects directly to that chosen SMTP server for a requested test email or Queue send. SMTP authentication sends the configured username and password/app password to that provider. A send transmits the sender and recipient addresses, subject, message body, standard email headers, and normal SMTP connection data. The SMTP password is stored encrypted in WordPress and is not sent to Stafflancer.

Terms and privacy depend on the SMTP provider selected by the administrator. Administrators should review that provider’s policies before connecting it.

Google OAuth2 and Gmail API

Purpose and data: an administrator can connect Gmail or Google Workspace with OAuth2. Google receives the configured OAuth client ID, redirect URI, requested scopes, one-time state and OIDC nonce values, authorization code or refresh token as required by the OAuth flow, and the credentials needed for token exchange. Queue sending sends the sender/recipient addresses, subject, message body, threading headers, and OAuth authorization to Gmail. Public signing keys are fetched from Google over HTTPS to validate connection identity. Diagnostics can query account identity. When mailbox-read access is enabled, Recipient Safety can issue bounded mailbox searches using sender/contact addresses, send-time boundaries, and/or a prior message ID to classify replies and delivery failures. Raw mailbox bodies are not stored by this scanner; only local suppression and bounded detection evidence are retained.

Google terms/privacy: https://developers.google.com/workspace/terms
Google API user-data policy: https://developers.google.com/terms/api-services-user-data-policy
Google privacy: https://policies.google.com/privacy

Microsoft OAuth2 and Microsoft Graph

Purpose and data: an administrator can connect Outlook or Microsoft 365 with OAuth2. Microsoft receives the configured OAuth client ID, redirect URI, requested scopes, one-time state and OIDC nonce values, selected tenant/account mode, authorization code or refresh token, and credentials needed for token exchange. Queue sending sends sender/recipient addresses, subject, message body, standard/threading headers, and OAuth authorization to Microsoft Graph. Microsoft OpenID configuration and public signing keys are fetched over HTTPS to validate connection identity. Diagnostics can query account identity. With Mail.Read enabled, Recipient Safety can query a bounded set of recent messages and process fields needed to classify replies and delivery failures; only local suppression and bounded detection evidence are stored.

Microsoft API terms: https://learn.microsoft.com/legal/microsoft-apis/terms-of-use
Microsoft privacy: https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/privacy/privacystatement

DNS resolver used by Inbox Diagnostics

Purpose and data: when an administrator runs inbox/domain diagnostics, PHP DNS lookups can check SPF, DKIM, DMARC, MX, TXT, and CNAME records for the configured sender domain. DNS requests contain only the domain or host name being checked and use the server’s configured DNS resolver. No contact list, email body, SMTP password, or OAuth token is included. Resolver terms/privacy depend on the site’s hosting or network provider.

Privacy and data

No analytics or telemetry is collected by Stafflancer Outreach or sent to Stafflancer. The plugin stores outreach workspace data in the site’s WordPress database, including contacts, groups, inbox configuration, sequence drafts, Queue records, send records, Recipient Safety suppressions, diagnostics, and OAuth2 setup/token metadata when configured.

Inbox Diagnostics can perform DNS lookups for the selected sender domain, including SPF, DKIM, DMARC, and MX records, using the site server’s configured DNS resolver. These lookups are performed only for inbox/domain diagnostics and are not sent to Stafflancer.

Sensitive SMTP secrets and provider OAuth credentials/tokens are stored using the plugin’s encrypted storage helpers. OAuth access is used only for the connected email-provider functions described above. Site administrators remain responsible for configuring their email providers appropriately, obtaining any required permissions or consent, and following applicable email, privacy, and anti-spam rules.

Source Code

The JavaScript and CSS source files for this plugin are included in this
download, under assets/js/ and assets/css/ respectively. The main application
script is assets/js/app-shell.js.

These files are maintained as plain JavaScript and CSS and are served directly
by the plugin. No compilation, bundling, or minification step is required to
modify or run them. Edit the included source files to make changes; no separate
source download or access to a development repository is required.

First-name repair

In Contacts, choose Repair missing names and upload the original CSV files. Preview exact email matches before filling blank first names. Existing names and all other contact details, groups, sequences and queue rows are kept. Download the report before leaving. Previews and reports are private to the current account and sign-in, expire after 24 hours, and expired preview records are removed when accessed or when that account creates a new preview. Completed repair outcomes are also recorded in the existing local audit log. CSV data is not sent to an external service. No hosting or cron configuration changes are required.
